texts.facts: The petitioners are aggrieved by the fourth respondent's orders seizing the R.O. water units under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (for short, 'the Act'), and the subsequent communication dated 28.12.2019 calling upon the petitioners to show cause as to why proceedings should not be initiated under the Act. It is undisputed that the fourth respondent has initiated the aforesaid proceeding for seizure and issued the impugned communication because the petitioners have not obtained necessary ISI Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards. texts.arguments: 2. The learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the first petitioner is a charitable trust and it has installed the R.O. water plant for the use of the community on a non-profitable basis and ISI certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards would be required only when water is sold as packaged drinking water, and if the facilities are set up for the benefit of the community for disbursing water in cans, such Certification would not be required. 3. A Division Bench of this Court in Lochamesh B Hugar v. Union of India and others reported in (2013) 2 KLJ 643, relying upon the provisions of Food and Safety Standards (Food Products, Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011 (for short 'the Regulations 2011), more specifically Regulation No. 2.10.8, has directed the Authorities to ensure that all necessary steps are taken to prohibit, prevent, manufacture and sale of packaged drinking water without Certification from the Bureau of Indian Standards with further directions. 4. The amendment reads as follows: "2.10.8 Packaged Drinking Water (other than mineral water) - 1. mean water, other than natural water that is likely to be used for human consumption ad that is offered or sold in packaged form, by whatever name it may be called, offered or sold" This Court, in the light of the amended provisions, in a similar matter in W.P.No.45574/2018 has held as under:- "Thus, from perusal of the amended Clause 2.10.8, it is evident that if the water is not sold for human consumption in packaged form, there is no requirement of obtaining the ISI Certificate.
